justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog Module handles physical and digital items; Digital Content Delivery Network / S3-compatible EU Object Storage holds digital assets; Circulation Module, Fines & Fees Module and Search Orchestrator Module add support. Gaps: no explicit physical/digital type model, and Catalog-to-Search indexing flow is vague.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Dedicated Search Engine (OpenSearch) with Index & Ranking Component and Search Orchestrator Module targets the 800 ms p99. PgBouncer, Redis Rate Limiter Filter, and Async Message Broker help. Gaps: no search result caching, no explicit scaling or latency budget, no load-test mechanism.
justifications.compatibility: Standard protocols are used: OpenID Connect via EU Identity Provider, REST/HTTPS to SEPA / Stripe EU API Payment Gateway, ISO ILL or mTLS REST for ILL partners, S3-compatible storage. API Gateway Versioning & Transformation Filter helps. Gaps: no catalogue standards such as MARC, Z39.50 or SRU.
justifications.usability: Web Application (SPA) serves patrons, staff and admins via Catalog Discovery Component, Circulation Desk Component and Admin Dashboard Component; Suggest & Spellcheck Component aids search. Gaps: no accessibility, localization or mobile channels, and no distinct patron self-service component.
justifications.reliability: Kafka multi-AZ replication, Local Persistence Layer offline circulation resilience, PgBouncer and rate limiting help. Gaps: no database replication or failover, single Core Services API monolith with no redundancy, no backup or DR, no circuit breakers.
justifications.security: Strong, explicit mechanisms: TLS 1.3, EU Identity Provider with Authentication/OAuth2 Proxy JWT validation, WAF, rate limiting, secure_pii Schema, pgaudit, Data Governance Interceptor, client-side encryption in Local Persistence Layer, SIEM audit streaming, and EU-only residency.
justifications.maintainability: Modular monolith with separate Catalog, Circulation, Fines & Fees and Search Orchestrator Modules, API Gateway filters, and separated containers. Observability via Prometheus exporters and W3C Trace Context. Gaps: Catalog-Circulation coupling, shared database, and Data Governance Interceptor covers only some modules.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes/Strimzi, Nginx/Envoy, PostgreSQL, OpenSearch and S3-compatible storage are open and replaceable. Gaps: no deployment diagram, no containerization or IaC for most containers, and vendor options left as either/or choices.

sensitivity_points: No search cache or replica/shard sizing specified
Search path passes through gateway and monolith
tradeoffs: Dedicated search index boosts latency but adds sync complexity
PERF-01.justification: Dedicated Elasticsearch and an orchestrator suit low-latency search, but there is no caching, scaling, replica or load-test mechanism. 2,000 concurrent users at P99 under 800 ms is plausible yet unproven.

sensitivity_points: Indexing load competes with queries on same cluster
Index lag bound of 5 minutes not monitored
tradeoffs: Async indexing protects search latency but gives eventual consistency
PERF-02.justification: Async ingestion into a separate index supports the 5-minute searchability goal. However, the Core-to-broker-to-index flow is not explicit (the Orchestrator reads Catalog directly), with no lag monitoring or isolation of indexing from queries.

sensitivity_points: Search cluster replication and failover not defined
Core Services' behaviour on search failure undefined
tradeoffs: Monolith simplicity vs lack of graceful degradation isolation
AVAIL-01.justification: Circulation uses PostgreSQL, so loans are independent of search, but no search replicas, failover, circuit breaker or fallback are specified. Kafka multi-AZ is mentioned, yet the Search Engine has no HA mechanism and the database has no stated HA.

sensitivity_points: No stated multiple instances or load balancing
Offline queue sync and conflict handling unspecified
tradeoffs: Offline persistence aids resilience but risks sync conflicts
AVAIL-02.justification: The SPA is client-side, so a portal instance failure mainly concerns static hosting and the gateway; no redundancy, load balancer or deployment is described. The offline queue protects staff circulation transactions, not patron loans, and there is no replica or HA design.

sensitivity_points: No provider adapter or integration component exists
Catalog Module couples physical and digital cataloguing
tradeoffs: Modular monolith eases deployment but weakens integration isolation
MOD-01.justification: No dedicated e-book provider integration or anti-corruption adapter exists. A new provider would likely modify Catalog Module and perhaps search ingestion, so changes are not confined to one component, though the modular monolith limits the blast radius.

sensitivity_points: Loan rules appear embedded in code
No rules engine or configuration store exists
tradeoffs: Hardcoded rules are simple but force redeployment for each policy change
MOD-02.justification: There is no rules engine, policy configuration store or tenant-specific rule mechanism. The Admin Dashboard is generic and Circulation Module has no configurable policy. Different loan rules would need code changes and redeployment.

sensitivity_points: Third-party EU vendors can still process data outside the EU
Interceptor covers only Catalog and Circulation modules
tradeoffs: External SaaS convenience vs strict control over residency
SEC-01.justification: EU-region services, a PII schema and a governance interceptor are good mechanisms. But Stripe, Twilio and Datadog are not guaranteed EU-only, the interceptor does not cover Fines or Search, and there are no infrastructure-level region controls, so enforcement is not by design.

sensitivity_points: No explicit object-level authorization on loan history
tradeoffs: Central gateway authentication vs per-resource authorization in modules
SEC-02.justification: Authentication, JWT validation, audit logging via the interceptor and pgaudit, and SIEM forwarding exist. However, no ownership or authorization check for patron-level loan access is defined, nor explicit logging of denied attempts.
